title: Geospatial-Intelligence Imagery Technician (GEOINT Tech)
raw_text:
8-350G. MOS 350G-- Geospatial-Intelligence Imagery Technician (GEOINT Tech)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
   c. MOS 350G. MOS 350G is an accession MOS. The feeder MOS is 35G.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
        (1) L8--Joint Operational Fires and Effects (in grade W3 only; personnel and positions).
(Effective 202610).
        (2) Q7--Information Collection Planner.
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
              (b) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI).
              (c) Complete the Geospatial-Intelligence Imagery Technician MI Warrant Officer
Basic Course (WOBC).
              (d) GPC-F certification is desired.
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Complete the resident MI Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
              (c) GPC-II certification is desired.                 (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Complete Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
   g. Duties.

        (1) WO1/CW2--
             (a) Directs Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Operations.
             (b) Projects GEOINT Requirements in Support of Unified Land Operations.
             (c) Directs GEOINT in Support of Joint Targeting; Coordinates GEOINT Tasking,
Collection, Processing, Exploitation, and Dissemination (TC-PED).
             (d) Manages GEOINT architecture.
             (e) Serves as advisor to the Command and staff on GEOINT operations, training,
policies, and procedures.
             (f) Manages GEOINT support to the Military Decision Making Process (MDMP).
             (g) Employs external capabilities, and integrates automation ISO GEOINT
operations.
             (h) May serve as the GEOINT Section OIC at any echelon.
             (i) May serve as the GEOINT Production Team Chief at any echelon.
             (j) May serve as a GEOINT Functional Manager.
             (k) May serve as a Collection Manager.
        (2) CW3--
             (a) Directs, plans, and performs duties shown in paragraph g(1).
             (b) Serves as the principal advisor to senior staff members, decision, and policy
makers on GEOINT operations, training, policies, and procedures.
             (c) Directs GEOINT operational coordination with Joint, Interagency,
Intergovernmental, and Multinational partners.
             (d) Develops and plans all GEOINT operations IAW applicable laws, policies and
treaties.
             (e) May serve as a Discipline Collection Manager at any echelon.
             (f) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
             (g) May serve as an OC/T at a CTC or MCTP.
             (h) May serve as a Detachment Commander.
             (i) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
             (j) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
             (k) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
        (3) CW4--
              (a) Manages, directs, plans, and performs duties shown in paragraph g(1) and g(2).
             (b) Serves as the principal advisor to senior staff members, decision, and policy
makers on GEOINT operations, training, policies, and procedures.
             (c) Directs GEOINT operational coordination with Joint, Interagency,
Intergovernmental, and Multinational partners.
             (d) Develops and plans all GEOINT operations IAW applicable laws, policies and
treaties.
             (e) May serve as a Discipline Collection Manager at any echelon.
             (f) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
             (g) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
             (h) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
             (i) May serve as HRC MI WO Assignments Manager.
        (4) CW5--
              (a) MI CW5s are proficient in the duties described in the duties paragraphs of one or
more MI WO MOSs.
             (b) MI CW5s are branch technical experts and master-level technical and tactical
experts who perform the primary duties of technical leader, manager, multidiscipline intelligence
integrator, and advisor.
             (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
             (d) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship,
advice, and counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers and have special
warrant officer leadership and representation responsibilities within their respective commands
             (e) Primarily support division, corps, echelons above corps, and major command
operations.
             (f) Advise commanders and branch assignment managers on the assignments and
placement of Military Intelligence warrant officers world-wide.
             (g) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform
other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities.
             (h) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
             (i) May serve on the Army Staff.
             (j) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief.
             (k) May serve as the MI WO Proponent.
             (l) May serve as the CCWO of the MI Branch.
             (m) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have competed the WO Senior
Service Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets h. Physical demand
rating and qualifications. Geospatial Intelligence Imagery Technicians must possess the following
qualifications:
             (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) -- Moderate.
             (2) A physical profile of 222211.
             (3) Normal color vision.
             (4) Distance vision correctable to 20/20 standard Snellen.
             (5) Qualifying Scores
                 a. Must have normal stereoscopic acuity (depth perception), and received a
“Pass” rating of “D,” “E,” or “F” on the Armed Forces Vision Test (AFVT) with or without
correction.

                b. Must have a minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power
Throw (PT) – 350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs, and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 36
shuttles in Physical Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).(6) The following grades are used to
code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4
equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade
tables:
            (a) Table 8-350G-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
            (b) Table 8-350G-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
